entries.message: Username and email fields offer the site's saved logins. On a page that asks for the username first, choosing one fills just the username, and the password step lists that login first.
Crest asks to save a password only when you typed it or chose one Crest made, and sent the form, never for a password a page or extension filled in, or after pressing a button such as Show Password.
Changing your password on a site offers to update the saved login, even when the form doesn't show your username.
Strong passwords follow the site's rules for length and characters, and wherever the site allows, they're three easy-to-type groups such as kvqhet-Mzawp7-rbnoxc.
Passwords save and fill on sites served from your own device, such as localhost.

On Mac and iPad, clicking a username, email or password field opens a popup under it with the site's logins, or says none are saved. Choose one with the arrow keys and Return, or open your passwords in Settings from the popup.
Use Strong Password shows the password it will fill and the site's rules for it, draws another with one click, and offers a random password with symbols where the site allows it.

Offers to save a password, address or card appear in the top right, where notices do. Not Now leaves a key in the address field so you can still save, and Never for This Site stops asking on that site.
On iPhone, Crest's strip above the keyboard offers the site's logins, one-time codes, your addresses and cards, or a strong password for a new account, beside the previous, next and Done buttons.
Suggestions point at sign-in fields inside a frame from the same site, and follow the page as it scrolls.

Settings › Passwords is now Autofill, with each Space's passwords and your addresses and payment cards. A password opens in an editor for its title, username, password, websites and notes, and the list searches, sorts, and moves, exports or deletes what you select.
Autofill marks reused, weak and plain-HTTP passwords, with a filter for each, and opens the site's own page for changing a password.
Password files carry notes and one-time code links when you import or export them, and an import says which column made a row fail.
Logins saved for an IP address written another way, such as 127.1, fill again.
Passwords can make one-time codes. Set one up from the site's QR code, a pasted key or link, an image, or the iPhone camera, and Crest offers the live code in the code field, across split fields too.

Crest fills addresses and payment cards into whole forms, menus included, and offers to save new ones you send. They're shared by every Space, and a card fills only after Touch ID or your device password.
